q: A liquid exerts pressure because of its weight.
e: True. A liquid exerts pressure because of its weight. Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column.

q: A liquid exerts pressure because of its volume.
e: False. The claim puts volume where weight belongs. A liquid exerts pressure because of its weight. Fluid pressure comes from weight.

q: The pressure in a liquid depends on the depth.
e: True. The pressure in a liquid depends on the depth. In a static liquid, pressure rises with depth as ρgh.

q: The pressure exerted by the liquid at the bottom surface is $p = \rho g h$.
e: True. The pressure exerted by the liquid at the bottom surface is p = ρ g h. In a static liquid, pressure rises with depth as ρgh.

q: The pressure exerted by the liquid is directly proportional to the height (or) depth of the liquid $h$ and the density $\rho$.
e: True. The pressure exerted by the liquid is directly proportional to the height (or) depth of the liquid h and the density ρ. Density is mass per unit volume, ρ = m/V.

q: The pressure exerted by the liquid is inversely proportional to the density $\rho$.
e: False. The pressure exerted by the liquid is directly proportional to the height (or) depth of the liquid h and the density ρ. Density is mass per unit volume, ρ = m/V.

q: The pressure exerted by the liquid is independent of the base area (cross-sectional area).
e: True. The pressure exerted by the liquid is independent of the base area (cross-sectional area). Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column.

e: False. The pressure exerted by the liquid is independent of the base area (cross-sectional area). Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column.

q: The true pressure at the depth $h$ in the liquid is $p = p_{\text{atm}} + \rho g h$.
e: True. The true pressure at the depth h in the liquid is p = patm + ρ g h. In a static liquid, pressure rises with depth as ρgh.

e: False. The claim puts - where + belongs. The true pressure at the depth h in the liquid is p = patm + ρ g h. In a static liquid, pressure rises with depth as ρgh.

q: The pressure in a liquid at a particular point acts equally in all directions.
e: True. The pressure in a liquid at a particular point acts equally in all directions. Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column.

q: The pressure in a liquid at a particular point acts only downwards.

q: Pressure at any point inside a liquid is the same in all directions.

e: True. If liquids of the same density are in containers all having the same height, the pressure exerted on their bases would be the same even though their weights and shapes are different. Density is mass per unit volume, ρ = m/V.
